name: unique-window-colors
description: Automatically adds a unique color to each window's activityBar and titleBar.

commands.title: Window Colors: Reset Colors in This Window
Window Colors: Remove Colors from This Window

enumDescriptions: Automatically matches your VS Code color theme (dark or light)
Removes the modified color settings from .vscode/settings.json
windowColors.theme.description:
Controls the color shades to blend with dark or light themes.  To switch betwen light and dark, you must first select 'remove' and reload VSCode to remove the settings, because they are not automatically overwritten.  This lets you modify the selected colors if you don't like what the extension picks.  

Reload the window for this to take effect (cmd-⇧-P, 'Reload Window')

windowColors.deleteSettingsFileUponExit.description: Remove Window Colors-managed color keys from workspace settings when the window closes. Other workspace settings are preserved. Set this in User Settings so the option does not remove itself.

windowColors.baseColor.description: HTML color name or hex color value (for example, 'whitesmoke' or '#ffffff'). Use the Window Colors: Set Base Color or Reset Colors command to change or remove it.

windowColors.colorTitleBar.description:
Apply the window's unique color to the top title bar.

Reload the window for this to take effect (cmd-shift-p, 'Reload Window')

windowColors.colorActivityBar.description:
Apply the window's unique color to the left activity bar.

Reload the window for this to take effect (cmd-shift-p, 'Reload Window')

windowColors.colorStatusBar.description:
Apply the window's unique color to the bottom status bar (all states: normal, debugging, no folder).

Reload the window for this to take effect (cmd-shift-p, 'Reload Window')

windowColors.neverColorThisWindow.description: Permanently skip coloring this window. When enabled, Window Colors will not apply or reapply any colors to this workspace.

scripts.test: npm run preview:check && npm run test:unit
